title: Drosophila Patronin: is the prion-like domain read as sequence or as condensation capacity?
objective: Decide whether the prion-like domain of Drosophila Patronin contributes to microtubule minus-end recognition through its specific primary sequence or through its capacity to condense, using evidence published before 2026-01-01.
coordinate_note: Construct numbering equals Patronin (UniProt A1ZAU8, 1630 residues) numbering plus 251 residues of N-terminal tag. The PrLD (Patronin 721-835) is construct 972-1086. Numbering in Atherton 2017 (fly CKK 1547-1689) refers to a different Patronin isoform and cannot be transferred directly.

hypotheses.question: Does the PrLD contribute to minus-end recognition at all, or does it only supply length and spacing between the other modules?
hypotheses.mechanism: If the PrLD merely separates the N-terminal CH region from the C-terminal coiled-coil, linker and CKK recognition module, an inert length-matched spacer should behave like the native domain. If any property of its sequence contributes, the spacer should resemble the deletion.
hypotheses.measurement: Each construct is read out in the same three ways: (i) purified mEGFP-Patronin on dynamic, polarity-marked microtubules by TIRF (minus-end to lattice intensity ratio, persistence of tracking at growing minus ends, protection from kinesin-13 depolymerisation); (ii) Drosophila S2 cells depleted of endogenous Patronin and rescued with an RNAi-resistant construct (minus-end foci, microtubule stabilisation, spindle length), with expression matched by fluorescence; (iii) a condensation covariate measured for every construct, namely droplet formation and FRAP of the purified protein with and without tubulin, and puncta and FRAP in cells at matched concentration. Spacer versus reference isolates sequence-dependent contribution at constant length; deletion versus spacer separates loss of the domain from loss of distance.
hypotheses.note: The spacer and the deletion are the shared negative baselines for the four hypotheses below; they are assigned here once.

hypotheses.question: Can an unrelated condensing disordered domain replace the PrLD, so that capacity to condense, and not the native sequence, is what is required?
hypotheses.mechanism: Condensation raises the local concentration and avidity of the recognition module on the minus-end lattice, so any disordered domain of comparable condensation strength should substitute whatever its primary sequence.
hypotheses.measurement: Each construct is read out in the same three ways: (i) purified mEGFP-Patronin on dynamic, polarity-marked microtubules by TIRF (minus-end to lattice intensity ratio, persistence of tracking at growing minus ends, protection from kinesin-13 depolymerisation); (ii) Drosophila S2 cells depleted of endogenous Patronin and rescued with an RNAi-resistant construct (minus-end foci, microtubule stabilisation, spindle length), with expression matched by fluorescence; (iii) a condensation covariate measured for every construct, namely droplet formation and FRAP of the purified protein with and without tubulin, and puncta and FRAP in cells at matched concentration. Restoration by the FUS LC swap in proportion to its measured condensation supports sufficiency of condensation capacity; a swap that condenses equally but does not restore recognition supports a sequence-specific role for the native domain.
hypotheses.note: FUS LC is Tyr-rich like the PrLD, so a rescue does not separate condensation from generic Tyr-mediated contacts with tubulin; an aromatic-poor condenser is the natural next round.

hypotheses.question: Does recognition depend on the linear order of the native PrLD, or only on its composition?
hypotheses.mechanism: A composition-preserving permutation destroys any linear motif or short-range pattern but keeps the number and overall spacing of stickers. It keeps function if composition-encoded condensation is what matters, and loses it if an order-specific motif is read out.
hypotheses.measurement: Each construct is read out in the same three ways: (i) purified mEGFP-Patronin on dynamic, polarity-marked microtubules by TIRF (minus-end to lattice intensity ratio, persistence of tracking at growing minus ends, protection from kinesin-13 depolymerisation); (ii) Drosophila S2 cells depleted of endogenous Patronin and rescued with an RNAi-resistant construct (minus-end foci, microtubule stabilisation, spindle length), with expression matched by fluorescence; (iii) a condensation covariate measured for every construct, namely droplet formation and FRAP of the purified protein with and without tubulin, and puncta and FRAP in cells at matched concentration. Shuffle versus reference at matched condensation. The shuffle was selected to match the native aromatic spacing so that condensation, not just composition, is the thing held constant; its measured condensation must be checked, not assumed.
hypotheses.note: A shuffle can change condensation and recognition independently, so it cannot be interpreted without the condensation covariate.

hypotheses.question: Is condensation by the PrLD aromatic stickers necessary for its function?
hypotheses.mechanism: Tyr and Phe residues are the main stickers of prion-like domains. Replacing all of them with Ser at constant length removes most sticker valence while leaving charge and the remaining composition close to native, so condensation should fall.
hypotheses.measurement: Each construct is read out in the same three ways: (i) purified mEGFP-Patronin on dynamic, polarity-marked microtubules by TIRF (minus-end to lattice intensity ratio, persistence of tracking at growing minus ends, protection from kinesin-13 depolymerisation); (ii) Drosophila S2 cells depleted of endogenous Patronin and rescued with an RNAi-resistant construct (minus-end foci, microtubule stabilisation, spindle length), with expression matched by fluorescence; (iii) a condensation covariate measured for every construct, namely droplet formation and FRAP of the purified protein with and without tubulin, and puncta and FRAP in cells at matched concentration. Loss of function that tracks loss of condensation supports necessity of condensation; retained function despite lost condensation argues against it.
hypotheses.note: Tyr could also be direct tubulin-contacting residues, so loss of function alone does not decide between condensation and sequence-specific contacts; it is read together with the swap and the shuffle.

hypotheses.question: Does fixed multivalency without liquid-like condensation substitute for the PrLD?
hypotheses.mechanism: Defined oligomerisation of CAMSAP-family proteins can by itself raise microtubule affinity of the CKK domain, so a tetramerisation motif may deliver the avidity that condensation would, without a disordered condensing domain.
hypotheses.measurement: Each construct is read out in the same three ways: (i) purified mEGFP-Patronin on dynamic, polarity-marked microtubules by TIRF (minus-end to lattice intensity ratio, persistence of tracking at growing minus ends, protection from kinesin-13 depolymerisation); (ii) Drosophila S2 cells depleted of endogenous Patronin and rescued with an RNAi-resistant construct (minus-end foci, microtubule stabilisation, spindle length), with expression matched by fluorescence; (iii) a condensation covariate measured for every construct, namely droplet formation and FRAP of the purified protein with and without tubulin, and puncta and FRAP in cells at matched concentration. A tetramer that restores recognition while showing no droplet formation separates multivalency from condensation capacity; one that fails argues that either condensation or the native sequence is needed.
hypotheses.note: Holding valence at four is an arbitrary choice; the native valence of Patronin in the assay is not known.

rationale.hypothesis: The native arrangement, tagged for purification and imaging, against which every PrLD edit is measured.

observations.finding: Purified Drosophila Patronin selectively binds microtubule minus ends and protects them from kinesin-13-induced depolymerisation in vitro, and stabilises minus ends in S2 cells.
observations.context: Drosophila S2 cells and purified protein, in vitro TIRF assays.

observations.finding: A highly conserved C-terminal domain and a more variable central domain cooperate to suppress minus-end dynamics in vitro, and both regions are needed to stabilise minus ends in S2 cells.
observations.context: Purified Patronin and CAMSAP fragments in vitro; S2 cells.

observations.finding: The isolated fly CKK domain tracks growing microtubule minus ends in vitro.
observations.context: Fly CKK fragment, dynamic microtubule assay; residue numbering in that paper differs from UniProt A1ZAU8.

rationale.uncertainty: The N-terminal mEGFP and His6 are an assumed, untested tag position: the CH domain lies near the N-terminus and the positively charged CKK tail near the C-terminus, and a tag at either end could change binding. A native-sequence or C-terminally tagged comparator is not in the library.

features.note: Absent from UniProt isoforms A and B.
UniProt disordered / compositional-bias annotation; contains a Gly11 run.
Approximate mapping of the central/CC region of Hendershott & Vale (2014).

rationale.hypothesis: Removes the assumed PrLD outright to establish how much recognition depends on the domain being present.
rationale.comparison: Against the reference for effect of loss; against the GS spacer to separate loss of the domain from loss of 115 residues of distance.
rationale.uncertainty: Deleting 115 residues shortens the tether between the N-terminal region and the C-terminal recognition module and removes any contribution of the assumed boundary choice; the boundary itself is computed here, so a phenotype could reflect part of the PrLD, or neighbouring sequence incorrectly included or excluded.
rationale.edit: Direct removal control for every other PrLD substitution.

features.note: Absent from UniProt isoforms A and B.
UniProt disordered / compositional-bias annotation; contains a Gly11 run.
Approximate mapping of the central/CC region of Hendershott & Vale (2014).

rationale.hypothesis: Replaces the PrLD with an inert flexible spacer of the same length to ask whether the domain acts only as a tether.
rationale.comparison: Against the reference at constant length, and against the deletion at constant spacer content.
rationale.uncertainty: A 115-residue GGS linker is treated as non-condensing and non-binding; that is conventional and was not tested. Gly and Ser are not equivalent spacers in prion-like sequences (Bremer 2022), so a very long GS stretch may itself alter compaction.
rationale.edit: Holds length constant while removing all PrLD sequence information.

features.note: Absent from UniProt isoforms A and B.
Condensation of FUS LC shown in vitro (Murthy 2019); not shown in this fusion.
UniProt disordered / compositional-bias annotation; contains a Gly11 run.
Approximate mapping of the central/CC region of Hendershott & Vale (2014).

rationale.hypothesis: Substitutes a well-characterised condensing domain of unrelated primary sequence for the PrLD.

observations.finding: FUS LC mediates liquid-liquid phase separation through multiple residue types, including Tyr and Gln, and stays disordered in the dense phase.
observations.context: Isolated human FUS LC in vitro; NMR, Raman and simulation.

observations.finding: Multivalent Tyr interactions in prion-like domains govern phase separation of FUS-family proteins; Gly favours fluidity and Gln/Ser favour hardening.
observations.context: FUS-family proteins in vitro and in cells.

observations.finding: Truncation and chimera versions of TPX2 were used to relate TPX2-tubulin co-condensation to nucleation efficiency.
observations.context: Xenopus TPX2 in vitro and in egg extract; chimera design not read.

rationale.comparison: Against the reference for sufficiency of condensation capacity, and against the GS spacer, which is length-matched to the native domain but not to this 163-residue insertion.
rationale.uncertainty: The insert is 48 residues longer than the PrLD, which changes tether length. FUS LC condensation in isolation needs high protein concentration in vitro and was reported to need the RNA-binding region in cells, so in this fusion it may not condense at all; the condensation covariate must be measured before a failure is interpreted. FUS LC is also Tyr-rich, so Tyr-mediated tubulin contacts remain possible.
rationale.edit: Heterologous condensing IDR chosen for near-zero net charge and a Tyr/Gln/Ser/Gly composition close to the PrLD, so that charge is not a confound.

features.note: Absent from UniProt isoforms A and B.
UniProt disordered / compositional-bias annotation; contains a Gly11 run.
Approximate mapping of the central/CC region of Hendershott & Vale (2014).

rationale.hypothesis: Keeps every PrLD residue but randomises their order, to test whether recognition reads a linear motif or only composition.

observations.finding: The number (valence) and patterning of aromatic residues set the phase behaviour of prion-like domains.
observations.context: hnRNPA1 prion-like domain, NMR, SAXS and simulation.

observations.finding: Tyr is a stronger sticker than Phe, and Gly and Ser are non-equivalent spacers in prion-like domains.
observations.context: Prion-like domain variants in vitro and in simulation.

rationale.comparison: Against the reference at identical composition; against the Tyr/Phe-to-Ser construct, which changes composition but not order.
rationale.uncertainty: The shuffle was picked from 60,000 random permutations (seed 20261116) for the same aromatic spacing (gap SD 4.48 vs 4.48 native; largest gap 20 vs 20), no longer homopolymer runs and no stronger charge blocks than native, and 13% positional identity to native. These are sequence-integrity checks, not predictions that it condenses like the native domain; one shuffle is one sample of order space.

variants.name: PrLD Tyr/Phe to Ser
variants.headline: All PrLD aromatics replaced by Ser

features.note: Absent from UniProt isoforms A and B.

Boundaries from a 60-residue sliding composition scan run here (Q/N/S/G/Y/T/P fraction, minus charge and hydrophobic penalties); the window with the highest score spans 751-810. In this construct all 14 Tyr/Phe residues are Ser.
UniProt disordered / compositional-bias annotation; contains a Gly11 run.
Approximate mapping of the central/CC region of Hendershott & Vale (2014).

rationale.hypothesis: Removes the sticker residues of the PrLD at constant length and charge to weaken condensation.

observations.finding: Phase separation of FUS-family proteins is primarily governed by multivalent Tyr interactions.
observations.context: FUS-family proteins in vitro and in cells.

observations.finding: Aromatic valence determines the extent of compaction and the full binodal of a prion-like domain.
observations.context: hnRNPA1 prion-like domain, NMR, SAXS and simulation.

observations.finding: A FUS LC variant with all Tyr changed to Phe forms aggregates and not droplets.
observations.context: FUS LC in vitro; the reason a Tyr-to-Phe swap is not used here.

rationale.comparison: Against the reference for the contribution of aromatic stickers; against the shuffle and FUS swap to separate condensation from Tyr-specific contacts.
rationale.uncertainty: Thirteen Tyr and one Phe become Ser; Ser promotes hardening of FUS-family condensates in Wang 2018, so the variant may gel or change material state rather than simply fail to condense. Whether the PrLD behaves like FUS LC is unmeasured; its aromatic content (14 in 115) is lower than FUS LC (24 Tyr in 163) and nothing here shows it condenses. Tyr that mediate direct tubulin contact would be removed together with the stickers.
rationale.edit: Fourteen single-residue substitutions, no change in length.

variants.headline: GCN4-pLI tetramerisation motif in GS flanks

features.note: Absent from UniProt isoforms A and B.
Oligomer state established for the GCN4-pLI peptide, not for this fusion.
UniProt disordered / compositional-bias annotation; contains a Gly11 run.
Approximate mapping of the central/CC region of Hendershott & Vale (2014).

rationale.hypothesis: Supplies a defined valence of four without a disordered condensing domain, at the same overall length as the PrLD.

observations.finding: An α-helix of CAMSAP3 mediates dimerisation, strengthens the microtubule affinity of the CKK domain and affects minus-end dynamics.
observations.context: CAMSAP3 and chimeras with CAMSAP1/2 in cells and in vitro.

observations.finding: Multivalency and disorder allow diverse microtubule-binding proteins to phase separate in vitro.
Residue identity at the a and d heptad positions of the GCN4 leucine zipper selects dimer, trimer or tetramer.
observations.context: GCN4 leucine zipper peptides in vitro.

rationale.comparison: Against the GS spacer, which has identical flank design and no oligomerisation motif, and against the FUS swap for valence versus condensation.
rationale.uncertainty: Tetramerisation of the isolated peptide is not shown for this fusion; a rigid coiled coil inside the tether may impose geometry the flexible PrLD does not, and a tetramer can increase avidity beyond anything native Patronin achieves. The pLI sequence was reconstructed from the GCN4 zipper by the published a/d substitutions and should be checked against the primary paper.
rationale.edit: Coiled-coil motif flanked by two 41-residue GGS segments, total 115 residues.

sites.label: PrLD Tyr/Phe residues (14)
sites.note: Candidate stickers inferred here from the composition of the assumed PrLD and the sticker grammar of other prion-like domains (Wang 2018; Martin 2020). Nothing measures their role in Patronin. Patronin numbering = construct numbering minus 251.

precedent_search.scope: PubMed, Europe PMC and web searches run 2026-11-16, limited to work published before 2026-01-01, for Patronin and CAMSAP condensation, prion-like or disordered-region contributions to minus-end recognition, IDR swaps in microtubule-binding proteins, and forward follow-up of Hendershott & Vale 2014 and Imasaki 2022. No pre-2026 study of a Patronin prion-like domain was found. One preprint on Patronin condensation dated October 2026 turned up and was excluded because it post-dates the cutoff; its content was not used in choosing any construct.

scale.higher_means: more conserved across this comparison set

method.comparison_set: UniProtKB members of UniRef50_A1ZAU8, the UniRef50 cluster containing A1ZAU8: the same protein in other species, clustered by UniProt at 50% identity with an 80% length-overlap requirement. ORTHOLOG level: scores answer what this protein needs.
method.alignment: multiple alignment by FAMSA via pyfamsa 0.7.0, projected onto reference coordinates by dropping columns where the reference is gapped. It can score positions that MAFFT leaves unscored, with weak support, so read per-position coverage alongside the score
method.weighting: Henikoff position-based sequence weights, computed over variable columns only
method.effective_sequences_definition: Neff = sum(1/n_i), n_i counting sequences at least 80% identical to sequence i over positions where both have a residue (itself included); pairs overlapping less than 50% of the reference are not counted as similar. Reported unnormalised and divided by reference length; normalisation is not standardised in the literature, so compare only against values computed the same way. This is NOT the sum of the Henikoff weights, which is rescaled to the sequence count by construction and therefore always equals it.
method.score: Jensen-Shannon divergence against Robinson & Robinson background, scaled by column occupancy (Capra & Singh 2007)
method.comparison_set_composition: 512 UniProtKB sequences of UniRef50_A1ZAU8: 406 Drosophila, remainder other Diptera (Glossina, Megaselia, Bactrocera, Stomoxys, Musca, Ceratitis, Lucilia), 33 species. This set reflects the genus and its close dipteran relatives, not metazoan CAMSAPs.
